chunks: The ledger (of their deeds) would be placed before them. Then you will see the sinners terrified at its contents, and say: "Alas, what a written revelation this, which has not left unaccounted the smallest or the greatest thing!" They will find in it whatsoever they had done. Your Lord does not wrong any one.
ai.seo_question: How does the Quran describe the presentation of the Book of Deeds on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the 'Book of Deeds' (Kitab al-A'mal) as a tangible, comprehensive record where every minor and major action is meticulously accounted for, emphasizing divine precision over human negligence. The sinners' exclamation, 'O woe to us!', reflects the shock of realizing that no deed was omitted, reinforcing the concept of 'Adl (Divine Justice) where God wrongs no one. This scene serves as a practical reminder for believers to maintain mindfulness (Muraqabah) of their actions, knowing that even the smallest deeds are preserved for the final reckoning.
